senses.definition: To poke or push suddenly with something pointed or with a short quick movement.
senses.example: Try not to jab the paintbrush against the paper.

senses.definition: A quick poke or short push.
senses.example: One jab with a pencil broke the paper cover.

senses.definition: To talk quickly and at length, sometimes making it hard for others to follow.
senses.example: We jabbered all the way to the park.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing for your upper body, usually worn over a shirt.
senses.example: I pulled on my jacket before walking to the bus stop.

senses.definition: A cover that wraps around something.
senses.example: The book’s paper jacket had a map printed on it.

senses.definition: One of several kinds of hares from North America with long legs and usually long ears.
senses.example: The jackrabbit bounded past the dry bushes.

senses.definition: Having a rough outline or sharp, uneven points.
senses.example: We cut a jagged edge to make the paper look torn.

senses.definition: A large wild cat of the Americas with strong jaws and usually a spotted coat.
senses.example: A jaguar's spots can make it hard to see among leaves and shadows.

senses.definition: A sweet spread made from cooked fruit and sugar.
senses.example: We put plum jam on our toast.

senses.definition: To get stuck or make something stick in a small space.
senses.example: The folded paper jammed inside the copier.

senses.definition: A crowd of cars or other things that are stuck and cannot move easily.
senses.example: We waited in a traffic jam near the bridge.

senses.definition: A container with a wide opening, often made of glass.
senses.example: We kept the buttons in a jar.

senses.definition: To shake or surprise in a sudden unpleasant way.
senses.example: The loud closing door jarred us awake.

senses.definition: Special words used by people in a particular job or activity.
senses.example: The coach explained the team's jargon before our first practice.

senses.definition: A plant often grown for its sweet-smelling white or yellow flowers.
senses.example: We could smell jasmine as we walked past the garden.

senses.definition: Cheerful and lively in the way someone looks or moves.
senses.example: She wore a jaunty yellow hat tipped to one side.

senses.definition: One of the bones or hard parts that hold the teeth or form a mouth.
senses.example: My lower jaw moved down as I opened my mouth.

senses.definition: One of the gripping parts of a tool.
senses.example: We slipped the bolt between the jaws of the wrench.

senses.definition: A bone that supports a row of teeth and forms part of the mouth.
senses.example: The fossil jawbone still held three teeth.

senses.definition: A bird in the crow family. Many kinds of jays are blue or have some blue feathers.
senses.example: A jay called from the tall pine.

senses.definition: A kind of music that began largely among Black musicians in the United States and often includes making up parts while playing.
senses.example: The trumpet player added her own notes during the jazz song.

senses.definition: Upset because you want what someone else has or fear losing their care or attention.
senses.example: I felt jealous when my brother got the bigger room.

senses.definition: Pants usually made of a strong cloth called denim.
senses.example: Ada wore jeans with a patch on one knee.

senses.definition: To laugh or shout at someone in an unkind way.
senses.example: Our coach told the crowd to cheer for the players without jeering at the other team.

senses.definition: An unkind shout or laugh aimed at someone.
senses.example: A jeer from the stands interrupted the announcement.

senses.definition: A smooth fruit spread made with fruit juice and sugar.
senses.example: I spooned grape jelly onto my bread.

senses.definition: A soft food that shakes when you move it.
senses.example: The lime jelly wobbled on the plate.

senses.definition: A small bean-shaped candy with a firm outside and a soft, chewy middle.
senses.example: I picked the purple jellybean from the bowl.

senses.definition: A soft sea animal that often has a see-through body shaped like a bell and hanging tentacles.
senses.example: A jellyfish drifted past the dock.

senses.definition: To move or pull with a quick, sharp motion.
senses.example: The sled jerked forward as the rope went tight.

senses.definition: A quick, sharp movement.
senses.example: One jerk on the cord started the little toy top.

senses.definition: A person whose job was to amuse a ruler and guests with jokes or tricks in earlier times.
senses.example: The jester wore bells that rang when he danced.

senses.definition: A narrow, fast stream of gas or liquid.
senses.example: A jet of water shot out from the fountain.

senses.definition: An aircraft that flies using one or more jet engines.
senses.example: The jet climbed over the clouds.

senses.definition: To shoot out or move in a very fast, narrow stream.
senses.example: Steam jetted out of a pipe at the old factory.

senses.definition: A narrow band of fast-moving air high in the sky.
senses.example: The plane flew with the jet stream and arrived sooner.

senses.definition: A wall or structure that sticks out from land into water, often near a harbor or river mouth.
senses.example: Waves splashed against the rocks on the jetty.

senses.definition: A valuable piece of stone, glass, or similar material that people wear or use to decorate things.
senses.example: A blue jewel shone on the ring in the shop window.

senses.definition: Things such as rings, bracelets, or necklaces worn for decoration.
senses.example: We made colorful jewelry by stringing wooden beads.

senses.definition: To move with quick, small shakes or to make something move that way.
senses.example: I jiggled the loose handle until the drawer opened.

senses.definition: A small power saw whose narrow blade moves up and down so it can cut curves.
senses.example: The woodworker used a jigsaw to cut a curved shape for the sign.

senses.definition: A picture puzzle made of many pieces that fit together.
senses.example: We worked on the jigsaw while we waited for dinner.

senses.definition: A puzzle made of pieces whose edges fit together, usually forming a picture when all the pieces are in place.
senses.example: We found the corner pieces of the jigsaw puzzle first.

senses.definition: To make a light ringing sound when small objects bump together.
senses.example: The keys jingled in my pocket.

senses.definition: A short, catchy tune that is easy to remember, often used in an advertisement.
senses.example: I caught myself humming the jingle from the radio.

senses.definition: Something or someone believed to bring bad luck.
senses.example: Some players joked that the empty bench was a jinx.

senses.definition: To bring bad luck, usually said as a joke or superstition.
senses.example: We teased him that guessing the score would jinx the team.

senses.definition: Feeling worried, excited, or unable to sit still.
senses.example: I felt jittery just before the spelling contest.

senses.definition: Work a person does, often to earn money.
senses.example: Mira’s summer job is to help at the library.

senses.definition: A task that needs to be done.
senses.example: My job after dinner is to wipe the table.

senses.definition: A person trained to ride horses in races.
senses.example: The jockey leaned forward as the horse ran down the track.

senses.definition: To run slowly at an easy, steady pace.
senses.example: We jogged around the track before practice.

senses.definition: To help someone remember something, usually in the phrase “jog your memory.”
senses.example: The picture jogged my memory about our trip.

senses.definition: Someone who runs at an easy pace for exercise.
senses.example: A jogger passed us on the trail.

senses.definition: To become part of a group or activity.
senses.example: I asked if I could join their game.

senses.definition: To connect things or come together.
senses.example: Two trails join beside the pond.

senses.definition: A place where bones meet.
senses.example: Your elbow is a joint that lets your arm bend.

senses.definition: One of a row of beams that support a floor or ceiling.
senses.example: We could see each wooden joist while the ceiling was being built.

senses.definition: Something said or done to make people laugh.
senses.example: Lee told a joke while we stood in line.

senses.definition: To say something for fun without meaning it seriously.
senses.example: I was only joking when I said I could eat a hundred pancakes.

senses.definition: Someone who likes to tell jokes or play tricks.
senses.example: My cousin is the joker in our family.

senses.definition: An extra playing card that has a special use in some games.
senses.example: I drew a joker and used it as any card I wanted.

senses.definition: Happy and cheerful in a lively way.
senses.example: Our jolly guide sang while leading us around the farm.

senses.definition: A sudden shake or movement.
senses.example: The wagon hit a rock and gave us a jolt.

senses.definition: To shake or move someone or something suddenly and sharply.
senses.example: A loud knock jolted me awake.

senses.definition: To write something down quickly and briefly.
senses.example: I jotted the time of the bus on a scrap of paper.

senses.definition: To write something quickly so you can remember it.
senses.example: Jot down the bus number before you close the map.

senses.definition: A book or file where you regularly record events, ideas, or observations.
senses.example: I kept a journal of the birds I saw from my window.

senses.definition: A publication about a particular subject, often written for people who study or work in that area.
senses.example: The librarian showed us a science journal with articles about plants.

senses.definition: Someone whose work is to find and share news with the public.
senses.example: A journalist asked the museum director why the exhibit mattered.

senses.definition: A trip from one place to another, often over a long distance.
senses.example: The train journey took most of the morning.

senses.definition: To travel a long distance.
senses.example: The story follows two friends who journey across a desert.

senses.definition: A strong feeling of happiness.
senses.example: The winning team cheered with joy.

senses.definition: A person or thing that brings happiness.
senses.example: Baking bread with Grandpa is one of my Saturday joys.

senses.definition: Full of happiness or bringing happiness.
senses.example: We made a joyous noise when the missing dog came home.

senses.definition: A short handle moved in different directions to control a machine or game.
senses.example: I moved the joystick left to turn the crane.

senses.definition: A special celebration marking a particular number of years since something began.
senses.example: The town held a jubilee one hundred years after the first train arrived.

senses.definition: A person who makes decisions in a court or picks winners in a contest.
senses.example: A judge scored each pumpkin in the carving contest.

senses.definition: To form an opinion after looking at or thinking about something.
senses.example: We judged which row of seeds had grown fastest.

senses.definition: A decision or opinion made after considering the facts.
senses.example: I trusted the lifeguard’s judgment that the waves were too rough.

senses.definition: The ability to make sensible choices.
senses.example: Rosa showed good judgment when she asked for help with the heavy table.

senses.definition: A sport developed in Japan in which people use holds and throws when competing.
senses.example: In judo class, the teacher showed us how to fall on a mat.

senses.definition: A container with a handle, often with a wide body and a narrow opening or pouring lip.
senses.example: We filled the jug with cold water.

senses.definition: To keep several things moving in the air by throwing and catching them.
senses.example: The performer juggled three cloth balls.

senses.definition: To handle several tasks at the same time.
senses.example: My dad juggles his work, the shopping, and getting us to school.

senses.definition: A performer who repeatedly tosses and catches several objects.
senses.example: The juggler kept three beanbags in motion.

senses.definition: Liquid from a fruit, vegetable, or other food.
senses.example: I squeezed the orange juice into a glass.

senses.definition: Full of juice or easy to squeeze juice from.
senses.example: The ripe orange was juicy and sweet.

senses.definition: A machine that plays a song you choose, often after you pay for it.
senses.example: My dad chose a song on the diner jukebox.

senses.definition: A group of things mixed together in a messy way.
senses.example: The drawer was a jumble of pencils and rubber bands.

senses.definition: To mix things out of order.
senses.example: The wind jumbled the pages of my notebook.

senses.definition: Much bigger than the usual size.
senses.example: We needed a jumbo bag to hold all the soccer balls.

senses.definition: To push off with your feet so your body goes into the air.
senses.example: Can you jump over the puddle without splashing?

senses.definition: To rise or change very quickly.
senses.example: The number of people in line jumped when the second bus arrived.

senses.definition: An act of leaving the ground suddenly by pushing off.
senses.example: Ruby made a big jump onto the bottom step.

senses.definition: A person or animal that jumps, especially in a sport.
senses.example: The high jumper cleared the bar by a few inches.

senses.definition: In the U.S., a sleeveless dress worn over a shirt. In Britain, a sweater.
senses.example: Mara wore a green jumper over a white shirt.

senses.definition: Nervous and easily startled.
senses.example: I felt jumpy after walking past the noisy construction site.

senses.definition: A place where two or more roads, tracks, or lines meet.
senses.example: We took the left path at the junction.

senses.definition: A place in a hot region where trees and other plants grow very thickly.
senses.example: Vines and broad leaves crowded the path through the jungle.

senses.definition: Lower in age, rank, or level than a senior group.
senses.example: My sister plays in the junior tennis league.

senses.definition: In U.S. schools, a student in the third year of high school or of a four-year college.
senses.example: My cousin became a high school junior in September.

senses.definition: An outdoor area where broken machines, metal, and other discarded things are stored.
senses.example: The old car was towed to the junkyard for its useful parts.

senses.definition: A group chosen to hear information and make a decision in a court case.
senses.example: The jury listened to the witnesses before making its decision.

senses.definition: Only or simply.
senses.example: I need just one more block to finish the tower.

senses.definition: A very short time ago.
senses.example: Your bus just left the corner.

senses.definition: Fair and based on what is right.
senses.example: Everyone thought it was a just way to choose a winner.

senses.definition: To give a good reason for an idea, choice, or action.
senses.example: We had to justify our answer by showing how we counted the squares.

senses.definition: To stick out farther than the things around it.
senses.example: A sharp corner of the rock jutted over the water.
